feed.title: Draft BIPs: anti-exfil signing for BIP340 and ECDSA, with PSBT fields

entry.title: Draft BIPs: anti-exfil signing for BIP340 and ECDSA, with PSBT fields
entry.summary:
A new approach has been developed to mitigate the risk of signing devices leaking their seed information through seemingly normal signatures. In standard digital signature workflows, each signature involves a randomly chosen nonce. However, if a device is compromised, it can intentionally select nonces that encode sensitive data, such as its internal seed, putting user funds at risk. To counter this threat, an anti-exfiltration protocol has been proposed, where the host system actively participates in generating each nonce and verifies the process, thereby reducing the opportunity for a malicious device to leak secrets.
While some hardware wallets have already implemented their own versions of anti-exfiltration measures, there has not yet been a universally accepted specification or a dedicated Partially Signed Bitcoin Transaction (PSBT) field for this functionality. Two draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs) aim to fill this gap. The first draft details the protocol compatible with BIP340 (Schnorr signatures used in Taproot) and ECDSA, specifying the responsibilities of the host when a device does not comply. The second draft introduces three new PSBT input fields to support this protocol. The design draws from Scheme 6 of Pieter Wuille’s 2020 overview, incorporating a sign-to-contract tweak to enhance security.
Recent developments include an experimental draft by Sjors Provoost for single-signer Taproot key-path signing, complete with implementations for hardware wallet interfaces and several devices. These implementations are expected to be brought into line with the new specification. Supporting resources include test vectors, a Python reference implementation, a C module for libsecp256k1, and a patch series for Jade’s sign_psbt function, although these have not yet been executed on actual hardware devices. Automated scripts are available to rerun most verification checks.
It should be noted that this protocol has not undergone formal cryptographic review or auditing. The related documentation explicitly discusses its limitations and lists areas where testing has failed or remains incomplete. Peer review and expert feedback on the security model are encouraged to strengthen the proposal. Further resources, including the repository and handbook, can be found at [https://github.com/AvilaLabs/anti-exfil](https://github.com/AvilaLabs/anti-exfil) and [https://anti-exfil.avilalabs.org](https://anti-exfil.avilalabs.org).
